# Federal Reserve lowers the target range for the federal funds rate

The Federal Open Market Committee cut its policy rate, citing a shift in the balance of risks.

The Committee said job gains have slowed and the unemployment rate has edged up but remains low, while inflation has moved up and remains somewhat elevated. It judged that downside risks to employment have risen. Christopher J. Waller voted against the action, preferring a larger cut.

fault.where: Christopher J. Waller voted against the action, preferring a larger cut.
fault.note: The source text names Stephen I. Miran as the dissenter; Waller voted for the action.
